title: The Core credit syncs to QuickBooks as a negative line
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with the Part sales -> Create & Edit permission, on the build under test.
  2. A customer to sell to exists; if none does, create one first: Customers -> New Customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  3. QuickBooks is connected for this shop with the one-time bookkeeping consent given.
  4. A part sale created on or after the release, carrying a part with a core charge. Seed it with these standard steps:
  5. ↳ Open Part Sales from the main menu and start a New Part Sale; select the customer (e.g. "4 Star Truck Repair").
  6. ↳ On the Parts tab, click Add Part; set the Description (e.g. "Water Pump") and the Sell Price to a test amount (e.g. $517.55).
  7. ↳ In the Core column of that row, enter a Core Charge greater than 0 (e.g. $79.99), then save the row.
  8. ↳ Order the part, then Receive it (special-order) or Pick it (inventory), so Return Core becomes available.
  9. Return the core (core row -> Return Core) so a Core credit row exists.
custom_steps:
1. Create Invoice on the sale and let it sync to QuickBooks.
  2. Open the resulting invoice in QuickBooks and find the Core credit line.
  3. Read its unit price, amount, product/service mapping, class and tax, and confirm it is a negative invoice line (not a credit memo).
  4. Compare the QuickBooks amount to the document's -$79.99 Core credit row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Core credit appears in QuickBooks as an ordinary negative invoice line with a unit price and amount of -$79.99 on a $79.99 core, using the same product/service mapping, class and parts tax treatment as the part row above it.
  • It is a negative line, not a QuickBooks credit memo, so it reduces the same revenue the part row increases; the QuickBooks amount equals the document's -$79.99 to the cent. (Only fee/discount rows are held back from the sync; a core row is a part row and is not.)

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-9667 (Founder Mode Batch #1); story SV-10262 (Story 1, Return a core on a part sale); Part Sales Update v1 PRD (Confluence 867434569), Story 1; design canvas boards Cores_*/Document_*; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

It is a negative line on the invoice, not a QuickBooks credit memo ... Only fee and discount rows are held back from the sync; a core row is a part row and is not”
